instrument: Statens vegvesen — Innbytte av førerkort fra land utenfor EU/EØS (national exchange scheme; the eligible origins are enumerated by the authority, not by treaty)
residence_condition: Applicant must have fast bopel (settled residence) in Norway, documented by a bostedsattest from Skatteetaten. If the licence was obtained while the holder was registered as resident in Norway, the holder must show either that they had fast bopel in the issuing country when it was issued, or that it was obtained during a temporary stay abroad lasting at least six months. Full førerrett is required on moving to Norway and valid førerrett when applying.
quote_original: Du kan få norsk førerkort hvis du har førerkort fra et av de landene utenfor EU/EØS som vi har nevnt her.
quote_translation: You can get a Norwegian driving licence if you have a driving licence from one of the countries outside the EU/EEA that we have named here.

instrument: Transportstyrelsen — Byta ut körkort från Förenade kungariket, Färöarna, Japan eller Schweiz
residence_condition: Applicant must be permanently resident in Sweden (permanent bosatt i Sverige), hold a valid licence, and meet the personal and medical requirements applying to a Swedish licence.
quote_original: Du kan byta ut ditt körkort från Förenade kungariket Storbritannien och Nordirland (Förenade kungariket), Färöarna, Schweiz eller Japan mot ett svenskt. Körkort från andra länder utanför EES kan inte bytas ut mot ett svenskt körkort.
quote_translation: You can exchange your driving licence from the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (the United Kingdom), the Faroe Islands, Switzerland or Japan for a Swedish one. Driving licences from other countries outside the EEA cannot be exchanged for a Swedish driving licence.

entries.note: Named as "Förenade kungariket Storbritannien och Nordirland". Unlike the other three, a UK licence stays usable in Sweden beyond one year of folkbokföring, so there is no one-year exchange deadline. Transportstyrelsen's page sets out the whole application (application form, health declaration and eyesight certificate for the light classes or a medical certificate for the heavy classes, the original foreign licence, and a certificate of validity from the issuing authority) and contains no driving-test step — but it does not say in terms that no test is required, so both test fields are left unrecorded rather than written as false.

Named as "Färöarna". Like the UK licence, a Faroese licence stays usable beyond one year of folkbokföring, so there is no one-year exchange deadline. Transportstyrelsen's page sets out the whole application (application form, health declaration and eyesight certificate for the light classes or a medical certificate for the heavy classes, the original foreign licence, and a certificate of validity from the issuing authority) and contains no driving-test step — but it does not say in terms that no test is required, so both test fields are left unrecorded rather than written as false.

Named as "Schweiz". Subject to the one-year deadline from folkbokföring. The surrendered licence is sent back to the issuing authority. Transportstyrelsen's page sets out the whole application (application form, health declaration and eyesight certificate for the light classes or a medical certificate for the heavy classes, the original foreign licence, and a certificate of validity from the issuing authority) and contains no driving-test step — but it does not say in terms that no test is required, so both test fields are left unrecorded rather than written as false.

Named as "Japan". Subject to the one-year deadline from folkbokföring. The validity certificate must be obtained from the Japanese embassy in Stockholm, and the surrendered licence is sent there. Transportstyrelsen's page sets out the whole application (application form, health declaration and eyesight certificate for the light classes or a medical certificate for the heavy classes, the original foreign licence, and a certificate of validity from the issuing authority) and contains no driving-test step — but it does not say in terms that no test is required, so both test fields are left unrecorded rather than written as false.

notes: Sweden's third-country annex is four entries long and the page states its own exhaustiveness: licences from any other non-EEA country cannot be exchanged. exchange_window_months is 12 because a non-EEA licence ceases to be valid in Sweden one year from the day of folkbokföring — but the page carves out the UK and the Faroe Islands, whose licences remain usable beyond that year, so the 12-month figure binds only Switzerland and Japan. Medical evidence is required in every case: a Hälsodeklaration plus an Intyg om synprövning for AM/A1/A2/A/B/BE, or a Läkarintyg for C1/C1E/C/CE/D1/D1E/D/DE. The original is surrendered — Japanese licences are returned to the Japanese embassy in Stockholm and UK, Faroese and Swiss licences to the issuing licensing authority. The test fields are null, not false: the page enumerates the entire procedure and contains no examination step, but it never states that no test is required, and writing false would invent a waiver. Page last updated 2025-08-14. EEA mutual recognition is handled on a separate Transportstyrelsen page and is deliberately not expanded here.

notes: This is by far the widest third-country annex in the region: Traficom publishes a named list of roughly 115 "sopimusvaltiot ja niihin rinnastettavat valtiot" whose licences can be exchanged, and the operative distinction is timing rather than origin. A contracting-state licence may be driven on for 2 years after moving permanently to Finland, and if the exchange is applied for inside that window, for a class other than BE/truck/bus, and while the entitlement is still valid, no driver's examination is required. Outside those bounds a full kuljettajantutkinto — theory AND driving test — is required, which is why exchange_window_months is 24: the window is what buys the test waiver. A medical certificate (lääkärinlausunto, valid 6 months) is required for every contracting-state exchange. The foreign licence is retained by Traficom and is returned only if the holder moves out of the country; a temporary Finnish licence is issued in the interim. Three list entries are not mappable to ISO 3166: "Jugoslavia" (a defunct state), "Kurdistan" (not a sovereign state, and Traficom does not say which issuing authority is meant), and "Yhdistynyt kuningaskunta ja siihen kuuluvat alusmaat", where the dependent territories are not enumerated. "Guayana" is read as Guyana, but the Finnish exonym is normally spelled "Guyana", so that mapping is inferred rather than stated. Classes are not recorded per origin because the page does not map them per country. Page last updated 25.6.2026. The EU/EEA list on the same page is deliberately not expanded here.

authority: Minister właściwy do spraw transportu; licences issued by the starosta
instrument: Ustawa z dnia 5 stycznia 2011 r. o kierujących pojazdami, art. 14 ust. 1 — consolidated text announced by Obwieszczenie Marszałka Sejmu z dnia 1 września 2025 r., Dz.U. 2025 poz. 1226
quote_original: Jeżeli prawo jazdy wydane za granicą nie jest określone w konwencjach o ruchu drogowym, o których mowa w art. 4 ust. 1 pkt 2 lit. a i b, dodatkowym warunkiem otrzymania polskiego prawa jazdy jest złożenie z wynikiem pozytywnym części teoretycznej egzaminu państwowego i przedstawienie uwierzytelnionego tłumaczenia zagranicznego dokumentu.
quote_translation: If the driving licence issued abroad is not one defined in the road traffic conventions referred to in art. 4(1)(2)(a) and (b), an additional condition for obtaining a Polish driving licence is passing the theoretical part of the state examination and producing a certified translation of the foreign document.

entries.origin_label_en: States whose national driving licence is defined in the 1949 Geneva or 1968 Vienna Road Traffic Convention
entries.note: Art. 14 ust. 1 imposes the theory-exam condition only where the foreign licence "nie jest określone w konwencjach o ruchu drogowym" (is not one defined in the road traffic conventions). A licence that is so defined is therefore exchanged on surrender of the foreign document, with no exam. Poland does not publish an enumerated country annex; the class is defined by convention membership, which is why no ISO code is given.

entries.origin_label_en: Any other state (licence not defined in the road traffic conventions)
entries.note: Art. 14 ust. 1: the additional condition is passing the THEORY part of the state examination and producing a certified translation. The statute names only "części teoretycznej egzaminu państwowego", so the practical part is recorded as not required on the face of the provision.

notes: Poland's third-country annex is defined by treaty membership, not by an enumerated country list, so it is recorded as two classes rather than as country rows — inventing a list of convention parties from a different instrument would be fabricating the annex. Art. 4 ust. 1 pkt 2 lit. a and b of the same act identify the two conventions: the Geneva Road Traffic Convention of 19 September 1949 (Dz. U. z 1959 r. Nr 54, poz. 321 i 322) and the Vienna Road Traffic Convention of 8 November 1968 (Dz. U. z 1988 r. Nr 5, poz. 40 i 44). Every exchange requires surrender of the foreign document to the issuing authority ("po zwrocie zagranicznego dokumentu organowi wydającemu prawo jazdy"). Only the THEORY part of the state examination is imposed on non-convention licences; the practical part is not, on the face of the provision. residence_condition, exchange_window_months and medical_certificate_required are left unrecorded because art. 14 itself is silent on all three — the general issuance conditions sit in art. 11, which was not read for this row. Art. 14 ust. 3-5 additionally allow the transport minister to set different, reciprocity-based conditions for the citizens of particular states by regulation; no such regulation was located, so no bilateral rows are claimed. The EU/Switzerland/EFTA-EEA carve-out in the same sentence is the mutual-recognition rule and is deliberately not expanded as annex rows.

entries.origin_label_en: States whose licence conforms to the Vienna 1968 or Geneva 1949 Road Traffic Convention model
entries.note: Sibling ministry page https://www.mdcr.cz/Zivotni-situace/Ridicske-prukazy/vymena-RP-mimoEU-CZ : "Řidičský průkaz vydaný cizím státem může být uznán k výměně za český řidičský průkaz pouze za předpokladu, že svým provedením bude odpovídat požadavkům (vzoru řidičského průkazu) stanovených Úmluvou o silničním provozu (Vídeň 1968) nebo Úmluvou o silničním provozu (Ženeva 1949)." That page lists only a valid identity document and the valid foreign licence — no examination and no medical certificate. Czechia publishes no enumerated country annex for this branch, which is why no ISO code is given.

Named exception on the non-conforming-licence page: for Japan only documents 1, 2, 3 and 6 are required (identity, proof of obvyklé bydliště, the valid foreign licence, and the medical certificate), plus a translation if needed — i.e. the přezkoušení z odborné způsobilosti is not required.
Named exception ("Korejská republika") on the non-conforming-licence page: only documents 1, 2, 3 and 6 are required, plus a translation if needed — no přezkoušení z odborné způsobilosti.
Named exception ("Spojené arabské emiráty") on the non-conforming-licence page: only documents 1, 2, 3 and 6 are required, plus a translation if needed — no přezkoušení z odborné způsobilosti.

entries.origin_label_en: Any other non-EU state whose licence does not conform to the conventions
entries.note: Exchange is available but the applicant must produce a "přezkoušení z odborné způsobilosti k řízení motorových vozidel" no older than 30 days, plus a medical certificate no older than 30 days. The ministry page does not split that re-examination into theory and practical components, so both fields are left unrecorded rather than guessed.

notes: Czechia's annex has two limbs and a named exception list, which is what makes it worth recording. Limb one: a non-EU licence whose FORM conforms to the Vienna 1968 or Geneva 1949 model is exchanged on production of an identity document and the licence alone — sibling ministry page https://www.mdcr.cz/Zivotni-situace/Ridicske-prukazy/vymena-RP-mimoEU-CZ . Limb two: a non-conforming licence is still exchangeable, but requires a přezkoušení z odborné způsobilosti k řízení motorových vozidel no older than 30 days plus a medical certificate no older than 30 days. Japan, the Republic of Korea and the United Arab Emirates are named as exceptions to limb two and need neither the re-examination nor the extra documents — only identity, proof of residence, the licence and the medical certificate. exchange_window_months is 3: the application must be made within 3 months of the day a Czech citizen returns to Czechia, or of the day trvalý pobyt or přechodný pobyt for more than 1 year is granted. medical_certificate_required is null at destination level because it is not uniform — required on the non-conforming limb and for the three named states, but not listed among the documents on the conforming limb. The original is surrendered on collection of the Czech licence and is sent to the issuing state, or held by the municipal office at the holder's request. A document marked "Provisional driving licence" is expressly not exchangeable, and an expired foreign licence cannot be exchanged at all. Non-conforming-licence page dated 02.08.2024; conforming-licence page dated 01.10.2020. EU mutual recognition is handled on a separate page and is deliberately not expanded here.

authority: SPF Mobilité et Transports / FOD Mobiliteit en Vervoer
instrument: Arrêté royal du 23 mars 1998 relatif au permis de conduire, art. 27, 2° (consolidated to 06-07-2026); the recognised-licence class is defined by art. 23, § 2, 1° of the loi relative à la police de la circulation routière
residence_condition: Art. 27, 2° a) and b) of the AR: the foreign licence must have been issued by the country where the holder had their normal residence at the time of issue, and must have been obtained BEFORE registration in the population/foreigners' register or the waiting register of a Belgian commune. Those two conditions do not apply to someone who proves they had student status for at least six months in the issuing country.
quote_original: 2° être titulaire d'un permis de conduire européen ou d'un permis de conduire étranger, visé à l'article 23, § 2, 1° de la loi; cette dispense ne vaut que pour la même catégorie
quote_translation: 2° hold a European driving licence or a foreign driving licence, referred to in article 23, § 2, 1° of the Act; this exemption is valid only for the same category
notes: What is established: the Belgian royal decree of 23 March 1998, read in its consolidated Justel version (dossier 1998-03-23/31, numac 1998014078, updated to 06-07-2026), exempts the holder of a foreign licence "visé à l'article 23, § 2, 1° de la loi" from BOTH the theory and the practical examination, for the same or an equivalent category, subject to the normal-residence and pre-registration conditions recorded above. Art. 25, § 2 of the same decree confirms the foreign document is handed over to the issuing authority and returned only against surrender of the Belgian licence. What could NOT be established: WHICH third countries fall inside art. 23, § 2, 1° of the loi. The decree itself carries no country annex — it delegates the definition to the loi relative à la police de la circulation routière, and the operative list is published by the SPF Mobilité et Transports rather than in the decree. What was tried: mobilit.belgium.be/fr/route/permis-de-conduire and .../permis-de-conduire-etranger, and belgium.be/fr/mobilite/permis_de_conduire/permis_de_conduire_etranger — all three sit behind an F5/Shape JavaScript bot challenge that returns HTTP 200 with a challenge shell and a "support ID" instead of content, so nothing quotable can be fetched and any URL cited from them would fail re-verification. vlaanderen.be has no page at the obvious path. The Justel copy of the loi itself was not retrieved. This is NOT an assertion that Belgium has no third-country exchange arrangement — the exemption in art. 27, 2° proves that it does. The annex membership is simply unlocated, and no origin rows are claimed. Note also that the ejustice host serves ISO-8859-1, so a UTF-8 fetch of this URL will mangle accented characters; the quote above is from a correctly decoded read.
